land.text: the Western Turkic tribes of the Chu valley and Zhetysu, whose leadership the Turgesh took over

predecessors.note: Page: the Turgesh 'preceded by' the Western Turkic Khaganate and the Second Turkic Khaganate (infobox); 'the leadership of the Western Turks was taken up by the Turgesh' (Western Turkic Khaganate page). The turks dossier (Cliopatria 'Turks', 666-698) carries the Western Turk remnant that ends in 699.

land.text: Suyab, captured in 703 (one of the Four Garrisons of Anxi on the Western Turkic Khaganate page)

predecessors.note: The two pages disagree on Suyab: Türgesh '703 he captured Suyab'; Western Turkic Khaganate 'from 679 to 719 Suyab was one of the Four Garrisons of Anxi'.

land.text: Zhetysu, which the Karluks conquered in 766 (Karluks page: 'formed a khanate under a Yabghu, occupied Suyab, and moved their capital there')

successors.note: Infobox: succeeded by the Karluk Yabghu and the Oghuz Yabgu State. The Karluk Yabghu State has no dossier of its own; qarlugs (Cliopatria 793-849, ia-01-f) is the nearest row.

capitals.name: Taraz
capitals.note: The infobox lists 'Capital: Taraz, Suyab' with no years; Taraz is placed first and Suyab was only captured in 703, so Taraz is the 699-702 seat by inference (confidence low). Coordinates are the gazetteer's Taraz.

capitals.name: Suyab (Ak-Beshim)
capitals.note: 'In 703 he captured Suyab'; Karluks 'occupied Suyab, and moved their capital there' in 766 (Karluks page). Gazetteer coordinates for Suyab; Taraz stays a second seat.

rulers.name: Wuzhile (Üch Elig)
rulers.note: The page's ruler list and infobox ('699-706: Üch Elig').

rulers.name: Suoge (Saqal)
rulers.note: 'In 706 his son Saqal succeeded him'; killed in 711 at the Battle of Bolchu.

rulers.name: Suluk
rulers.note: The ruler list says 716-738; the text says 'In 714 the Turgesh elected Suluk as their khagan'. 711-715 is the Second Turkic overlordship or interregnum.

rulers.name: Kül Chor
rulers.note: Submitted to the Tang in 740, killed a Tang puppet in 742, captured and executed by the Tang in 744.

rulers.name: Ata Boyla
rulers.note: The page gives '750s-766' (list) and 'c. 750-766' (infobox), which overlaps Yibo (749-751) and Tengri Ermish (753-755); placed after 755 here.

correction.text: years only: the Mongolian Plateau shape of 692-704 belongs to the Second Turkic Khaganate (682-744), which has no dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers: second-turkic-khaganate); the Turgesh draw nothing in 692-698. [fx-22 fix 2026-11-01: the verdict only changed the years, but the compiler drew the unchanged Cliopatria shape for 699-704, giving the Turgesh the whole Mongolian Plateau (10,651 cells) in 699 and removing it in 705; the keyframe now ends in 698, before the dossier starts, so the Taraz core (turgesh_699) and the 703 gain are the only land of 699-704.]

keyframe_review.note: 692-704, 2.68 M km2, bbox 87.7-120.8 E: the Mongolian Plateau (75 percent of the plateau, all of the Orkhon valley) and part of the Altai, nothing in Zhetysu. The Second Turkic Khaganate page puts the Turks of the Orkhon there ('Frontiers were defined by the Tannu Ola, Altai, and Tarbagatai ranges' in 698-701; the khaganate was founded by Ilterish in 682 and lasted until 744) and the Türgesh page makes the Turgesh a state only from 699 ('established a khaganate in 699'). The shape is the Second Turkic Khaganate under a wrong label (the probable swap with the Cliopatria row 'Turks'). Neither page gives an area, so no infobox figure can be compared. [fx-22 2026-11-01: from/to set to 692-698. Pages opened: Second Turkic Khaganate page: the khaganate 'lasted from 682 to 744' and 'was centered on Otuken in the upper reaches of the Orkhon River'; Turgesh page: the Turgesh 'established a khaganate in 699' and in 703 'set up his authority on the territory from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq'; neither page puts the Turgesh on the Orkhon.]

correction.text: a Taraz core: the infobox capital, before the 703 capture of Suyab

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 699-702. The page says only 'established a khaganate in 699' (Wuzhile) and lists Taraz and Suyab as capitals; Suyab is captured in 703, so the first four years are drawn as a Taraz core only (soft, confidence low). Cliopatria has nothing for these years under this name.

correction.text: from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq (the page's own span: Chach, the Semirechye/Zhetysu steppe with Suyab and Talas, Dzungaria around Beshbalik, the Turfan oasis)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 703-704 (Cliopatria's first Türgesh shape is the Mongolian Plateau, marked wrong above). 'In 703 he captured Suyab and set up his authority on the territory from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq.' About 0.9 M km2 against Cliopatria's 4.03 M km2 for 705 (the page gives no area to compare).

correction.text: from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq (the page's own span: Chach, the Semirechye/Zhetysu steppe with Suyab and Talas, Dzungaria around Beshbalik, the Turfan oasis)

keyframe_review.note: 705-723, 4.03 M km2: the Cliopatria shape is the Second Turkic Khaganate's Mongolian Plateau (9,025 cells), Altai and Kazakh steppe plus the Turgesh lands and Transoxiana (1,067 cells). Corrected to the page's span 'from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq' (about 0.9 M km2, 3,595 cells: Semirechye, Dzungaria, Chach, Turfan). Transoxiana is not direct land: in 719 its rulers petition 'the Chinese and their Turgesh overlords' (vassal pair in the ledger). Qapaghan beat the Turgesh at the Boluchu River in Dzungaria in 711 (contest in the ledger). The Cliopatria 'Turks' shape (692-717) lies wholly inside this one, so the two rows double-draw Zhetysu in 705-717.

correction.text: from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq (the page's own span: Chach, the Semirechye/Zhetysu steppe with Suyab and Talas, Dzungaria around Beshbalik, the Turfan oasis)

keyframe_review.note: 724-740, 4.04 M km2. Same correction as 705 until 735; from 736 the Dzungarian end is lost: 'the Tang made an alliance with the Umayyads against Suluk in 735' and 'Suluk's Türgesh forces were later defeated at Beshbalik in 736' (Battle of Talas page). From 736 use the corrected shape of turgesh_736 (to 744) and turgesh_745 (from 745).

The page gives no territorial detail for the civil war of 738-744 or for Tang suzerainty from 740 (the Tang dossier should carry that).

The page dates the civil war between the Black (Kara) and Yellow (Sary) factions from Suluk's murder, Kül Chor's submission to the Tang in 740, the Tang puppet killed in 742 and Kül Chor's execution in 744, but gives no border.

correction.text: Zhetysu (Semirechye), which the Karluks conquered in 766

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 745-765 (Cliopatria's 'Türgesh' row ends in 749; it draws 'Turks' 750-756 and the Uyghur Khaganate over Zhetysu). The page ends the khaganate only in 766: 'In 766 the Karluks conquered Zhetysu and ended the Turgesh Khaganate', and lists khagans to 766 (Ata Boyla). Drawn as Zhetysu alone, soft; the page is silent on 745-765. The lands beyond Zhetysu (Chach, Dzungaria, Turfan) are taken out from 745, the year after the Tang executed Kül Chor (Cliopatria's Tang shape of 752 holds 1,289 Dzungaria cells and all of Turfan).

region.text: a Taraz core (infobox capitals Taraz and Suyab)

ledger.note: 699: Wuzhile founds the Turgesh khaganate. Wuzhile, 'a leader of a Manichaean consortium', 'established a khaganate in 699'. The page gives no place for the first four years; the infobox capital Taraz is the drawn core.

region.text: from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq (the page's own span: Chach, the Semirechye/Zhetysu steppe with Suyab and Talas, Dzungaria around Beshbalik, the Turfan oasis)

ledger.note: 703: Wuzhile takes Suyab and the span from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq. 'In 703 he captured Suyab and set up his authority on the territory from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq.' The Western Turkic Khaganate page calls Suyab a Tang Anxi garrison from 679 to 719 and has Tang control of the area last 'until the time of An Lushan's rebellion in 756', so the counterpart is the Tang (the two pages disagree on how long Suyab stayed Tang); the Türgesh page adds that in 703-706 Wuzhile drove out Böri Shad, a Tang protégé.

region.text: Dzungaria around the Boluchu River and Beshbalik

ledger.note: 711: Tonyukuk beats the Turgesh at the Boluchu River in Dzungaria. 'Tonyukuk defeated the Türgesh at the Boluchu River in Dzungaria' (Second Turkic Khaganate page); the Türgesh page: 'Qapaghan Khagan defeated the Turgesh in 711 in the Battle of Bolchu, and killed both Saqal and Zhenu.' The Turks then fought near Samarkand in 713-714 and 'failed to take Beshbalik'.

region.text: Dzungaria around the Boluchu River and Beshbalik

ledger.note: 715: Qapaghan is assassinated and the Second Turkic push into Dzungaria ends. The page dates the assassination (715) and a civil war of 716-717; it does not say that the Turgesh recovered the land, and the Türgesh page has Suluk elected khagan in 714. The end year is inferred.

region.text: Sogdia, Ferghana and the other principalities of Transoxiana

ledger.note: 719: the rulers of Transoxiana appeal to their Turgesh overlords. 'in 719, when the Transoxianian sovereigns sent a petition to the Chinese and their Turgesh overlords for military aid.' The page does not date the start of the overlordship; 719 is the first year it is attested.

721: Kül Chor beats the Umayyads near Samarkand. 'Turgesh forces, led by Kül Chor, defeated the Caliphate army commanded by Sa'id ibn Abdu'l-Aziz near Samarkand', after attacks 'beginning in 720' (the Türgesh page puts the battle in 720).
728: Suluk takes Bukhara. The page says Suluk 'in 728 took Bukhara'. The Day of Thirst (724) and the Battle of the Defile (731, Türgesh page) are battles without a dated change of ground.

732: the Umayyads recover Samarkand and Bukhara. 'By 732, two large Arab expeditions to Samarkand managed, if with heavy losses, to reestablish Caliphal authority in the area.' Suluk then gave up Samarkand and left Bukhara, withdrawing north.

region.text: Sogdia, Ferghana and the other principalities of Transoxiana

ledger.note: 732: Caliphal authority returns to Sogdia and the Turgesh overlordship ends there. The page does not say what became of the Ferghana and Chach rulers; the Tang and the Karluks claim Transoxiana in the 739 entry of the Karluks page.

736: the Tang, allied to the Umayyads since 735, beat Suluk at Beshbalik. 'the Tang made an alliance with the Umayyads against Suluk in 735. Suluk's Türgesh forces were later defeated at Beshbalik in 736.' The page does not say that the Tang kept the ground; the loss follows Cliopatria's Tang shape of 752, which holds Dzungaria.

743: Nasr ibn Sayyar secures Transoxiana for the caliphate. 'Taking advantage of his death, Nasr recovered most of Transoxiana by 743.' Suluk had been murdered in 738 ('Next year, Suluk was murdered by his general Kül-chor with Chinese support'; year inferred) and the Turgesh were in civil war.

minus.text: from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq (the page's own span: Chach, the Semirechye/Zhetysu steppe with Suyab and Talas, Dzungaria around Beshbalik, the Turfan oasis)

region.text: Chach, the Dzungarian and Turfan lands outside Zhetysu

ledger.note: 745: the Tang hold the lands beyond Zhetysu after executing Kül Chor. 'Kül-chor was captured and executed by the Tang in 744' (Kül-chor had submitted to the Tang in 740). The page gives no border for 745-765; the land beyond Zhetysu (Chach, Dzungaria, Turfan) is Tang, Abbasid or Uyghur in Cliopatria's rows of 752-760, so the Turgesh are drawn on Zhetysu alone (confidence 1: bridging).

766: the Karluks take Zhetysu. 'After overrunning the Türgesh in Jetisu, the Karluk tribes formed a khanate under a Yabghu, occupied Suyab, and moved their capital there.' The Türgesh page: 'In 766 the Karluks conquered Zhetysu and ended the Turgesh Khaganate.'
766: the Karluks end the Turgesh Khaganate. Infobox 'Disestablished: 766'. Cliopatria ends the row in 749; the page lists khagans to 766.

wars.name: Battle of Bolchu (Second Turkic-Turgesh war)
wars.outcome: Qapaghan and Tonyukuk beat the Turgesh and kill Saqal and Zhenu (711); the Turks fight near Samarkand in 713-714 and fail to take Beshbalik; Qapaghan is assassinated in 715.
wars.note: The Türgesh page: 'Qapaghan Khagan defeated the Turgesh in 711 in the Battle of Bolchu'.

wars.name: Tang-Turgesh wars of 708-717

zones.text: the northern rim of the Tarim, Kucha and Aksu

wars.outcome: Saqal attacks Kucha (708) and beats a Tang force (709); Tang sends Ashina Xian (appointed 712); in 717 Xian leads Tang-allied Karluk forces, defeats the Turgesh and drives them out of the Tarim Basin.
wars.note: Türgesh page: '708: Saqal attacked the Tang city of Qiuci (Kucha). 709: Saqal inflicted a defeat on the Tang.' Western Turkic Khaganate page: 'In 717, Xian led Tang-allied Karluk forces to defeat the Turgesh'.

wars.name: Battle of Aksu
wars.outcome: Tang victory: General Tang Jiahui defeated the Arab-Tibetan-Turgesh attack on Aksu and Uch Turfan on 15 August 717.

wars.name: Turgesh-Umayyad wars in Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Turgesh victories near Samarkand (721), the Day of Thirst (724), Bukhara (728) and the Defile (731); Arab recovery by 732; Suluk defeated at Kharistan in winter 737 and murdered in 738; Nasr recovered most of Transoxiana by 743.
wars.note: Türgesh page: '720 Turgesh forces led by Kül-chor defeated Umayyad forces led by Sa'id ibn Abdu'l-Aziz near Samarkand'; '731 ... Battle of the Defile'; '737 ... Battle of Kharistan'.

wars.name: Tang-Umayyad campaign against Suluk
wars.outcome: The Tang ally with the Umayyads against Suluk (735); his forces are beaten at Beshbalik (736).

wars.name: Turgesh civil war and Tang suzerainty
wars.outcome: After Suluk's murder the Black (Kara) and Yellow (Sary) factions fight; Kül Chor of the Yellow beats Tumoche of the Black, submits to the Tang in 740, kills a Tang puppet in 742 and is captured and executed by the Tang in 744. No border is given.

wars.name: Karluk conquest of Zhetysu
wars.outcome: The Karluks overrun the Turgesh in Zhetysu, occupy Suyab and end the khaganate.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout. The one named line is the page's span 'from Chach to Turfan and Beshbaliq' (703); the Sogdian frontier with the Umayyads moves with each campaign (721-743) and is not a line.

notes: Label swap, settled by the shapes: Cliopatria's 'Türgesh' (692-749) is the Mongolian Plateau (75 percent of it, all of the Orkhon valley) plus the Turgesh lands from 705; the Mongolian part is the Second Turkic Khaganate (682-744), which the Second Turkic Khaganate page dates and places on the Orkhon and which has no dossier or Cliopatria row of its own (second-turkic-khaganate needs one; its 692-749 land is this row's Mongolia, and the Uyghur Khaganate takes the plateau from 744/750). Cliopatria's 'Turks' (666-756, dossier turks) lies wholly inside the 705-717 Türgesh shape (1,176 of 1,435 Semirechye cells in both), so in those years the two rows double-draw Zhetysu; this dossier keeps the land from 699 and turks ends in 698. The Cliopatria 750-756 'Turks' shapes are reviewed as wrong in the turks dossier. The correction replaces the 4.03-4.04 M km2 shape with the page's own span (about 0.9 M km2); the page gives no area, so the infobox comparison is impossible. Transoxiana is a vassal tint 719-732 and a contest zone 721-743 against the Umayyad Caliphate, not direct land; no page gives the Turgesh a direct holding there beyond Bukhara in 728-732. Open points: (1) the Tang dossier should carry Tang suzerainty from 740 (Kül Chor submits) to 744 (Kül Chor executed) with this state as counterpart, and the 703 loss of Suyab and 736 gain of Beshbalik; (2) no page gives the Turgesh border between 745 and 765, so turgesh_745 is Zhetysu alone while Cliopatria draws the Uyghur Khaganate over Zhetysu in 760 (Karluks page: the Karluks took Zhetysu only in 766); (3) the Western Turkic Khaganate page puts Suyab under Tang until 719, the Türgesh page has the Turgesh take it in 703; (4) the ruler list overlaps in the 750s (Ata Boyla) and has Suluk 716-738 against 'elected in 714'; (5) capitals Taraz and Suyab carry no years on the page. Karluk Yabghu State (756-940, infobox successor) has no dossier: qarlugs (ia-01-f) is the nearest row.
